content:
In his latest speech, Trump ignored all context and immediately gave his critics a ready-made 'viral' moment to exploit.

Trump spoke on Tuesday to unveil America.gov, a new AI-powered government website, during which he said 'nothing compares' and claimed 'my friends, some serious tech people, after looking at it these past few days, said it's incredible'.

Trump continued: 'They said, "This is one of the best things your government has ever done." I don't see it that way. I think it's great. But someone said, "Sir, this will be the single greatest achievement you've done in government." I said, "I don't think so, but it's really great, okay?" It's just another thing, just another thing.'

Trump also mimicked someone telling him: '"Sir, sir, undoubtedly, this will be the most——'"

Then, returning to his own voice, Trump said: 'If this is the greatest thing I've done in all this time, that means I've been a terrible president, I'll tell you that. But you know what, it's really great.'

What Trump clearly meant to express was that if this new website — intended as a digital portal for government services and which has already debunked his false claims about the 2020 election — turns out to be his greatest achievement, then his overall performance in office would count as a failure.

But the remark 'I've been a terrible president' was quickly clipped and spread widely on social media, predictably going viral online.
